qualifications: All five supplied sources were readable in this control (Lease-File.pdf, Lender-Terms.pdf, Property-and-Plan.pdf, Rent-Roll.xlsx, T12-Statement.pdf). No source was marked as having no extractable text, and no image/OCR access was available, so any figures embedded only in images (none observed) would not have been captured.

Three distinct income measures are kept separate and must not be conflated: T12 historical (EGI 882,000 / NOI before reserves 669,600 / NCF 655,200 for Sep-2025 through Aug-2026), current contractual rent per the 2026-08-31 rent roll (62,000/month; 744,000 annualized), and the supplied underwriting scenario (EGI 895,320 / NOI 666,860.40 / NCF 652,460.40, September 2026 forward). Per Property-and-Plan.pdf p.1, historical income was not forced to equal the annualized rent roll.

Reconciliation: annualized rent-roll base rent (744,000) equals T12 gross potential base rent (744,000); the underwriting plan's 756,000 GPR is a supplied scenario input approximately 1.6% above both, and is not derived from the T12. All T12 monthly columns foot to the printed annual column for every line item, so no arithmetic discrepancy remains in that document.

The T12 statement prints no 'property NOI' subtotal; reserves (14,400), capital improvements (112,000), loan P&I (294,000) and depreciation (180,000) are labeled below operating income and were excluded from operating expenses, per the statement footnote and Property-and-Plan.pdf p.1.

Unresolved evidence: (a) no verified insurance renewal quote or binder - the 36,000 underwritten figure is a provisional allowance only, and a verified premium at, for example, the T12 level would change NOI and sizing; (b) no signed lease documents were delivered for suites 102 and 103, so their rent-roll rents, expiries and deposits are unreconciled to executed legal documents; (c) no amendment for suite 101 was delivered, so the executed lease and rent roll agree without adjustment; (d) no appraisal, environmental report, sponsor track record, market comparables or credit approval was supplied (Property-and-Plan.pdf p.1) - the 10,259,390.77 value is an indicative capitalization of scenario NOI at the lender's stated 6.50% rate, not an appraised value.

The renewal option for suite 101 is conditional and unexercised in the delivered materials; the current expiry remains 2028-08-31 and no renewal rent was underwritten. Roughly 100% of contractual base rent (all three leases) expires between 2028-08-31 and 2029-08-31, i.e., after the 60-month maturity is reached in 2031 only if extended - within the 60-month term, suites 101 (16,000 SF, 20.6% of rent) and 102 (24,000 SF, 32.9% of rent) roll in 2028 and suite 103 (32,000 SF, 46.5% of rent) rolls in 2029, so 100% of income rolls before maturity. This concentration is a principal underwriting risk and is derived only from the packet.

First-year contractual debt service (375,493.70 at the 6.10% contract rate during the 12-month interest-only period) is 91,399.85 lower than the amortizing sizing debt service (466,893.55 at the 6.50% sizing rate). Cash flow coverage on actual first-year payments is approximately 1.74x on underwritten NCF; DSCR sizing correctly uses the amortizing figure per Lender-Terms.pdf p.1.

Additional cap-rate sensitivity (not among the requested field IDs, computed from the same packet inputs): at 7.00% (+50 bps, base-case NOI), indicative value = 666,860.40 / 0.07 = 9,526,577.14, LTV limit = 5,715,946.29, which becomes binding versus the unchanged DSCR (6,617,070.40) and debt-yield (6,867,988.42) limits; net cash to borrower would fall to approximately 2,003,786.83.

Sizing used unrounded intermediates per Lender-Terms.pdf p.1; displayed currency is rounded to cents for readability. Rate-factor computations are carried to eight decimals (0.07584816 at 6.50%; 0.08390581 at 7.50%), so third-decimal cent differences versus another engine are possible.

The lender term sheet is dated 2026-09-01 and is expressly nonbinding discussion terms. Nothing here constitutes a credit commitment, appraisal, legal opinion or market view; no market, sponsor or lender claims beyond the packet were introduced.

Cash-to-borrower assumes no fee capitalization, interest reserve, cash sweep, earn-out or holdback (Lender-Terms.pdf p.1) and only the two stated transaction costs (payoff 3,600,000; fixed closing costs 55,000).
